pll1d20c2-d1e3477.summary: Cites Augustine against Maximinus: the one who says 'All that the Father has is mine' has nothing less than the Father; if he had less power, not all the Father's would be his. So the Son has as much power as the Father and is equal, since the receiver cannot be unequal to the giver.
claims: The Son has all that the Father has, including power.
The Son is equal to the Father in power.

pl-l1d20c2.summary: Gives Augustine's first argument against Maximinus from John 16:15 ('All that the Father has is mine'): if the Son had less power, not all the Father's would be his. So the Son has as much power as the Father and is equal, since the receiver cannot be unequal to the giver.
claims: All that the Father has belongs to the Son.
Therefore the Son has as much power as the Father.
The one who receives all cannot be unequal to the giver.
